chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Yaʿqūb ibn Shuʿayb, from Ḥarīz, or from one who narrated it, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I said to Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام: The people of Kūfah narrate from ʿAlī عليه السلام that he used to command wudu (ablution) before ghusl (ritual bath) from janabah.
He said: “They have lied against ʿAlī عليه السلام. We did not find that in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام.
Allah, the Exalted, said: “And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves.”

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: janabah, the state of major ritual impurity
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ghusl (ritual bath), the major purification required after janabah
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the minor ritual purification mentioned here as preceding ghusl
key_terms.فَاطَّهَّرُوا: then purify yourselves, the Qur’anic command to perform purification
key_terms.كَذَبُوا: they lied, meaning a false attribution was made
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: the Book of ʿAlī, a written source of transmitted rulings associated with Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: Is wudu (ablution) required before ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah according to Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith rejects the report that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام instructed wudu (ablution) before ghusl (ritual bath) for janabah. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that this was not found in the Book of ʿAlī عليه السلام and cites the Qur’anic command requiring purification from janabah. The narration is significant in establishing a jurisprudential ruling on ritual purity directly grounded in the Qur’an and the transmitted teaching of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
